subject: history
title: Causes of War Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the key words historians use to explain why wars start.
meta_desc: GCSE History Causes of War foundations — MAIN causes, alliances and the road to conflict.
final_note: You learned the vocabulary historians use to analyse the causes of war.

concepts.def: Glorifying armed forces and building up weapons
A formal agreement to support another country
Building or controlling an empire abroad

walkthroughs.body_html:
The MAIN causes of WWI: Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism, Nationalism.

Europe in 1914 was an arms race tied together by treaties — a small spark could pull everyone in.

On 28 June 1914, Archduke Franz Ferdinand was assassinated in Sarajevo by Gavrilo Princip.

Within six weeks the alliance system dragged Austria-Hungary, Germany, Russia, France and Britain into war.

The Treaty of Versailles left Germany angry. Hitler rearmed and took the Rhineland, Austria and the Sudetenland.

Britain's policy of appeasement hoped to avoid war. When Hitler invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, that hope ended.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT one of the MAIN causes of WWI?
options: Militarism
Alliances
Industrialism
Nationalism
Building up weapons
Giving in to demands to avoid war
Joining an alliance
Invading a neighbour

mcqs.q: Why did the League of Nations fail to prevent WWII?
options: The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
The League failed because no countries joined it.
The Schlieffen Plan failed because it tried to invade Russia first.
Absence of the US, requirement of unanimous decisions, no armed force of its own, weak responses to Manchuria (1931) and Abyssinia (1935), and great-power self-interest.

mcqs.q: Why did Britain win the Battle of Britain?
options: The RAF won because Spitfires were better than any German aircraft.
Radar, the Dowding command system, home advantage in pilot recovery, German tactical errors (switching to bombing cities), and adequate fighter production.
Hitler called off the attack to invade the USSR immediately.
The Schlieffen Plan failed because it tried to invade Russia first.

mcqs.q: Why did the Schlieffen Plan fail in 1914?
options: The Schlieffen Plan failed because Britain entered the war.
The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
The Schlieffen Plan failed because it tried to invade Russia first.
Belgian resistance delayed the German advance; Russia mobilised faster than expected; Moltke weakened the right wing; and the French rallied at the Marne.
